To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) strengths use is a proactive behavior that can be stimulated through personal initiative, (b) strengths use is related to positive work outcomes (e.g., work engagement, job performance, organizational citizenship behavior), and (c) strengths use has a positive impact on employee well-being (e.g., job satisfaction, life satisfaction, psychological well-being)

(a) employees who use their strengths are more engaged and perform better; (b) employees use their strengths more when they are given the chance to do so; (c) employees who use a wide range of their strengths are more satisfied; and (d) strengths use is a positive and important phenomenon, but not a panacea.

1) Strengths use is positively related to job performance, work engagement, and well-being; and 2) Strengths use can be increased by personal initiative, organizational climate, and opportunities for learning and development.

the question how people can be helped to use their strengths at work.
the question of how employees can be helped to develop their strengths.
the question of how people can flourish in their work, and how organizations can support employees in their quest for flourishing.
